key_insight: A marker-less, mobile multi-camera capture system enables accurate 3D reconstruction of hands and manipulated objects in unconstrained, real-world environments, bridging the gap between studio datasets and in-the-wild scenarios.
problem_solved: Existing hand–object interaction datasets are mostly captured in controlled studio settings, which limits environmental diversity and causes poor generalization of models to egocentric, real-world manipulation scenes.
method: Mobile, marker-less multi-camera capture rig designed for near-unconstrained movement and natural scenes.
Multi-view reconstruction pipeline that jointly recovers 3D hand poses and object shapes/poses from captured footage.
Creation and release of a large in-the-wild dataset with annotations for training and benchmarking hand–object 3D understanding models.
impact: Provides realistic training data and standardized benchmarks that improve generalization of 3D hand–object models for egocentric vision, benefiting AR/VR, robotics, and human–computer interaction research.
visual_elements: System diagram of the mobile marker-less multi-camera rig and example capture setup
Side-by-side visualizations of input video frames and reconstructed 3D hands + objects
Pipeline flowchart: capture → multi-view reconstruction → joint hand/object fitting → annotations/dataset
Dataset diversity montage showing varied scenes, lighting, poses, and object types
paper_title: SHOW3D: Capturing Scenes of 3D Hands and Objects in the Wild
paper_authors: Patrick Rim, Kevin Harris, Braden Copple, Shangchen Han, Xu Xie
